summary: Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) was a sinology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, the University of Tokyo (1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Yün-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. A research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953, he later served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990) and taught James G. Mullens, Albert Welter, Kang-nam Oh, and Yu-kwan Ng.
Zack Beer is a student in Buddhist studies and Indology, with studies attested in 2026 at both the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the University of California, Berkeley.

Zalman Movshevich Dymshits (1921–1990) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Moscow State University (~1945–1950), he taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1953–1954) and became a professor at Moscow State Institute of International Relations in 1954.

Zarawar Khan specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1929) under Pe Maung Tin (~1925–1929) and later studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zayn Kassam is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. At Pomona College from 1995, she served as department chair, Associate Dean for DEI, and John Knox McLean Professor. She also directed the Pacific Basin Institute and the Institute of Ismaili Studies.
Zdeněk Materna (1900–1944) was an Indology scholar who studied at the Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague (~1919–1925), earning a Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý (1920–1925).

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (-2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held an attested post at the College of Charleston in 2001.

Zellig Harris (1909–1992) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University, and taught Ernest Bender.

Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen.
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1931 to 1934 under teacher Naoshiro Tsuji.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner who studied at the University of California and under Jōshin Kasai, Richard Baker, and Mel Weitsman. She was co-abbess at the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002) and taught Taigen Dan Leighton.
Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He taught Eshin Nishimura and held posts at Otani University (~1948) and Hanazono University.
Zenno Ikuno (b. 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his master's at Taisho University. He served as professor and professor emeritus at Taisho, president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014), and held posts at Shukutoku and Dongguk universities.

Zennosuke Tsuji (1877–1955) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1938), University of the Sacred Heart (~1948), and Rissho University (~1949–1954).

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. Educated at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities, he served as Kyoto University's president (1949–1961), director of Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972), and president of Kacho Junior College (1973).

Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi and served as lecturer (attested 1976) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, with affiliations also attested at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Tokyo Rissho Junior College.
Zerkxis Bhandara is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who holds a religious studies post and is attested as a graduate student in 2026 at the University of California, Santa Barbara.
